_comment: English names of the instruments an international court cites, mapped onto the corpus document that carries their text (rule:configured-by-data). Keyed by target URI local part; `source` names the corpus half it lives in. `names` are the forms a court actually writes, longest-first at match time so a full title beats a short form that prefixes it. `articles` says whether the target's artifact carries per-article anchors, which decides whether a citation can be pinned to `#A<n>` or only to the instrument. `names_sv` are the Swedish citation forms the lagrum engine matches in Swedish body text ("artikel 24 i barnkonventionen"); reader-facing Swedish labels stay in each source's own names.json and may differ. coe/005 carries no names_sv because coe/data/names.json already feeds the Swedish matcher. A name may be shared by several instruments: "the Geneva Conventions" names all four, and common article 3 really is an article of each, so it resolves to four references rather than to a guess at which one was meant. `anchor` is the prefix the target's artifact mints an article under, "A" unless stated: the Hague Regulations are an *annex* to Convention (IV), so their article 42 is #Annex42 and pointing at #A42 dangles. `last_article` is the highest article the target actually carries, read off its artifact: a citation past it is a misbinding, not a provision, and falls back to naming the instrument. `numerals` is the form the target anchors its articles in: the Genocide Convention runs Article I to XIX and a citation written "article 1" must still reach #AI, where minting #A1 pointed at nothing. `generic_names` are forms too generic to name an instrument on their own -- every treaty family numbers its protocols, and the corpus holds a 'Second Additional Protocol' in three of them -- so a generic name only matches where `generic_context` (a regex) also occurs within lib.treatyref.CONTEXT_WINDOW characters of it: 'Additional Protocol II to the Geneva Conventions' binds, the bare 'Second Additional Protocol to this Convention' on a CoE page does not.

instruments.note: The 1899 Convention (II) annexes Regulations with the same title (icrc/150), so no name here tells the two apart. The 1907 text is the target because it is the one in force and the one the courts cite: of 72 mentions across the ICC and ICJ corpora, 32 write "1907" and 40 name the Regulations alone. None writes "1899". A decision that does needs its own entry against icrc/150 -- naming both, the way "the Geneva Conventions" names four, would file 40 citations against a convention no court in this corpus applied.
